curation.notes: Paper describes nonequilibrium alchemical free energy calculations (NEQ) for absolute binding free energies, not mechanical pulling. Classified as AA-ENH due to ensemble of fast alchemical transitions. Protocol mode is 'other' (alchemical perturbation). Event type is B-single (ligand unbinding). Topology is ligand-pocket. Observables are binding free energies, not force-extension. Reduction models are Crooks Fluctuation Theorem and Jarzynski inequality. Assumptions include pathway_rate_invariant and one_d_reaction_coordinate. Benchmark throughput reported as ~200 ns/day on a single GPU. Experimental comparison to binding affinity measurements present.

curation.notes: Paper describes a coarse-grained molecular dynamics model of the axon membrane skeleton (actin rings connected by spectrin filaments) used to compute stiffness via radial expansion. No traditional force-extension pulling of a single molecule; the 'pulling' is a quasi-static radial expansion of the entire network to measure pressure vs. strain. Classified as CG-GO due to the use of simplified, structure-based potentials (harmonic, LJ, FENE) for a cytoskeletal network. Event type is A-stretching (measuring elastic modulus of the network). Topology is parallel (spectrin filaments act as parallel load-bearing elements between actin rings). Experimental comparison is to the authors' own AFM indentation measurements.

benchmark.hardware: duals P4 XEON, 3.0 GHz (FSB 800 MHz) and XEON 2.4 GHz; SGI Origin3800 and on 64-bit processors Intel Itanium2

curation.notes: Paper describes equilibrium MD simulations of RNA kissing complexes, not pulling simulations. No force-extension data or analytical models applied. Skeleton filled based on paper content. No pulling protocol present.

class_id.quote: Explicit solvent molecular dynamics simulations (in total almost 800 ns including locally enhanced sampling runs) were applied with different ion conditions and with two force fields (AMBER and CHARMM). p. 1

protocol.mode.quote: Standard (MD) and LES simulations (LES) performed with the AMBER force field. Table 1

protocol.temperature_K.quote: Constant temperature of 300 K was maintained using the Berendsen weak-coupling algorithm. p. 5

protocol.monovalent_salt_mM.quote: This corresponds to ionic strength of ∼0.2 M (considering the number of ions and size of the water box). p. 6

protocol.ions_treatment.quote: All systems were neutralized by Na+ or K+ ions using the Xleap module of AMBER. p. 4

protocol.solvent.quote: Box of TIP3P water molecules was added to a distance of 12 Å on each side of the solute. p. 4

sampling.timestep_fs.quote: The standard simulations were carried out using the particle mesh Ewald technique (68) with 9 Å nonbonded cutoff and 2-fs integration time step. p. 5

molecule.name.quote: We focus on flanking base positions in multiple x-ray and NMR structures of HIV-1 DIS kissing complexes and kissing complex from the large ribosomal subunit of Haloarcula marismortui. p. 1

molecule.oligomer_state.quote: The DIS stem-loop is nine-nucleotides-long (residues A272-A280) and contains a six-nucleotide (nt) self-complementary sequence in the loop. p. 1

force_field_or_params.quote: We test different ion conditions and two force fields (AMBER parm99 (65) and CHARMM27 (60,61)). p. 9

benchmark.hardware.quote: AMBER simulations were run on duals P4 XEON, 3.0 GHz (FSB 800 MHz) and XEON 2.4 GHz. CHARMM simulations were run on SGI Origin3800 and on 64-bit processors Intel Itanium2. p. 7

stated_assumptions.quote: The nonpolarizable pair additive force field represents the ions as van der Waals spheres with atom-centered point charges.
